data.why: A town's sewer ends in a pipe mouth over a river with a rubber duck floating in it; the plant is dug in the cut between town and river, so the sewage's own path (screen, settling tank, aeration tank, digester, ultraviolet channel, outfall) is the order of the story, seen in section. Each problem is a visible consequence (brown plume round the duck, brown water past the screen, murky tank, sludge on the floor), and the end returns to the pipe mouth pouring clean water past the duck.

surprises.claim: At a treatment plant, bar screens catch rags and trash before the sewage reaches the tanks.
surprises.search: wastewater treatment bar screen removes rags trash preliminary treatment

surprises.claim: In a primary settling tank, heavy solids sink to the bottom and scum floats to the top.
surprises.search: primary clarifier solids settle scum floats wastewater

surprises.claim: In an aeration tank, blown-in air feeds bacteria that eat the dissolved waste.
surprises.search: activated sludge aeration tank bacteria consume organic matter air

surprises.claim: Ultraviolet light is used to kill germs in treated wastewater before it is released.
surprises.search: ultraviolet disinfection treated wastewater kills pathogens before discharge

ideas.idea: if you pipe your toilets into a river, you have a sewer
but the river turns brown around the duck
so you dig a plant, where a screen catches trash
but past the screen, the water stays brown
so the tank stays still, and solids sink
but the water above the solids stays murky
so you blow in air, and bacteria eat waste
but the bacteria settle as sludge on the floor
so you pump sludge to a digester, where gas burns
but past the digester, germs still ride out
so ultraviolet lamps kill the germs before the outfall
open the outfall, and clean water reaches the duck
congratulations, you have built a sewage treatment plant

sentences.text: If you pipe your toilets into a river, you have a sewer.
But the river turns brown around the duck.
So you dig a plant, where a screen catches trash.
But past the screen, the water stays brown.
So the tank stays still, and solids sink.
But the water above the solids stays murky.
So you blow in air, and bacteria eat waste.
But the bacteria settle as sludge on the floor.
So you pump sludge to a digester, where gas burns.
But past the digester, germs still ride out.
So ultraviolet lamps kill the germs before the outfall.
Open the outfall, and clean water reaches the duck.
Congratulations, you have built a sewage treatment plant.
